title: World No. 1 Rumesh Tharanga’s javelins damaged on aeroplane
content:
Rumesh Tharanga, the world’s No.1 ranked javelin thrower, had his javelins damaged on an aeroplane while they were being transported back from a World Athletics competition.

Tharanga, 23, took gold at the World Ultimate Championship in Budapest, Hungary on Sunday before flying back to Sri Lanka the following day.

He posted a photo on his Instagram stories on Tuesday of a collection of snapped javelins, accompanied by the caption “Bad luck”. This was followed by the same photo captioned with: “Thank you Turkish Airlines”.

Turkish Airlines has been contacted by The Athletic for comment.

The Sri Lankan sports minister Sunil Kumara Gamage confirmed five of Tharanga’s javelins had been damaged in transit. In quotes carried by News Wire, he confirmed that the government of Sri Lanka would cover the cost of replacing Tharanga’s javelins, with the athlete a top hope to win the country’s first Olympic gold medal at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.

“Our government will continue to stand behind our athletics star and his Olympic dream,” Gamage said.

Tharanga is due to compete in the Asian Games this month, with the men’s javelin competition beginning on September 26.

Tharanga won the men’s javelin title at the World Ultimate Championship — the inaugural biennial competition organised by World Athletics in between World Championship years — with a throw of 91.09m on Sunday. It represented his third major title of 2026, following his golds at the Commonwealth Games and Diamond League.

He is the Sri Lankan national record holder, having thrown a personal best of 92.62m at the 2026 Golden Gala in Rome in June. His throw then is the furthest in the world this year, and the best since Arshad Nadeem’s 92.97m in the 2024 Olympic final.

Tharanga is targeting a maiden Olympic gold medal for Sri Lanka at LA 2028. The country has won two silver medals across 19 appearances at the Olympics since first competing at the Games in 1948.

“I hope to win an Olympic gold medal for Sri Lanka in 2028,” Tharanga told the Olympics official website this month. “My primary thought is to break the world record. Let’s see; I definitely keep in mind that I need to bring home a medal that Sri Lanka doesn’t have yet.”
